job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: In our economics class today, we simulated how a multinational company (MNC) operates. We imagined a firm based in India that sets up manufacturing units in Vietnam and Brazil to reduce costs and access local markets. This proved that MNCs do not just produce goods in their home country, but strategically spread operations globally. We then discussed the role of the Indian government in the 1991 reforms. By removing trade barriers, the government actively shaped the economy, proving that globalisation is not an uncontrollable natural force but a policy-driven process. We also examined the World Trade Organization (WTO). While it sets rules for international trade, we discovered that developed nations often exert more influence than developing ones, meaning it is not a perfectly democratic body where everyone holds equal power. Finally, we looked at local toy makers. When trade barriers were removed, these small producers faced intense competition from cheaper imported goods, showing that liberalisation does not automatically benefit every local business. This activity highlighted that while globalisation integrates markets, its outcomes depend heavily on government regulations and the power dynamics between nations.

items.evidence: We imagined a firm based in India that sets up manufacturing units in Vietnam and Brazil to reduce costs and access local markets.
items.q: An Indian firm opens factories in Vietnam and Brazil. What does this show about MNCs?
options: They spread production across several countries
They send finished goods from India only
They make goods at home, then sell abroad
They let local firms make all their goods
items.explain: The firm set up units abroad to cut costs and reach local markets, so MNCs spread production globally.

wrong.why: thinks MNCs produce only in the home country
thinks goods are made in one place then shipped
mixes up who owns and runs the factories

items.evidence: By removing trade barriers, the government actively shaped the economy, proving that globalisation is not an uncontrollable natural force but a policy-driven process.
items.q: Why does the 1991 reform show that globalisation can be shaped?
options: Government policy opened the economy to trade
Trade barriers fell on their own over time
The WTO ordered India to remove them
Every country opened its markets equally then
items.explain: The government removed trade barriers by choice, so globalisation follows policy decisions and is not an uncontrollable force.

wrong.why: thinks globalisation happens naturally without policy
thinks the WTO forced India to remove barriers
thinks fair globalisation means equal opening

items.evidence: While it sets rules for international trade, we discovered that developed nations often exert more influence than developing ones, meaning it is not a perfectly democratic body where everyone holds equal power.
items.q: A developing country disagrees with a WTO rule. What is most likely to happen?
options: Richer nations may have more say in the outcome
Its vote counts the same as every other
The rule changes because each country is equal
The WTO leaves trade rules to each country
items.explain: Developed nations often have more influence in the WTO, so a developing country may not get its way.

wrong.why: thinks the WTO gives all countries equal power
thinks one country can change rules alone
thinks the WTO sets no rules for trade

items.evidence: When trade barriers were removed, these small producers faced intense competition from cheaper imported goods, showing that liberalisation does not automatically benefit every local business.
items.q: After import barriers fall, why might a small Indian toy maker struggle?
options: Cheaper imported toys compete for its buyers
Foreign firms refuse to buy its toys
Its toys can no longer be sold abroad
Only large firms are allowed to make toys
items.explain: Cheaper imported goods create intense competition, so small local producers may lose customers when barriers are removed.

wrong.why: thinks trade only means exporting goods
thinks removing barriers helps every local producer
thinks small firms are banned from making goods
